rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Mich, the fish-form sea deity of Kamchatka.
ANATOMY: One living fish-form deity: one fish head, two eyes, one scaled body, ordinary fins and one tail; no human limbs, horns, crown or invented hybrid [mich-c01, mich-c04]
MOMENT: Surges through a heavy curve of ocean water toward the close viewer while a surrounding school of smaller fish swims toward driftwood by the shore
POWER: Sends fish to shore to fetch wood: smaller fish stream toward floating wooden fragments; ocean displacement is physical habitat movement, not glowing magic [mich-c02, mich-c05]
SCALE & CAMERA: close low camera, subject occupies most of the square, sharp diagnostic anatomy, no unclaimed gigantic size; all required countable features separated and visible.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one dominant warm raking dusk light, deep walnut shadows and antique-gold highlights, high contrast, atmospheric depth without magical glow.
SURFACE: tactile natural skin, fur, feathers, scales or cloth as appropriate, painterly material detail, never plastic.
SETTING: Sea and rocky shore of Kamchatka [mich-c01]
MOOD: imposing and awe-inspiring or threatening according to documented character, never cute, calm or decorative.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, pseudo-writing, rune, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. No decorative symbols or inscriptions.
